title: Flow Diagram
description: A directed flow diagram: nodes, parallel branches and rounded connectors laid out from the JSX tree, pannable by drag, wheel or arrow keys when it overflows.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Flow: nodes progress along the inline axis or top to bottom.

props.name: align
props.description: Flow: cross-axis alignment of nodes of different sizes.

props.name: padding
props.description: Flow: space around the diagram inside the canvas, in pixels.

props.name: canvas
props.description: Flow: measure the canvas and enable panning, wheel scrolling and the scrollbars.

props.name: onOverflowChange
props.description: Flow: called when the diagram starts or stops overflowing its canvas.

props.name: aria-label / aria-labelledby
props.description: Flow: names the canvas group; name it whenever it can pan (it is then focusable).

props.name: className
props.description: Flow: classes for the canvas (a border, a height).

props.name: Flow.Node: render / disabled / id
props.description: A custom element instead of the default card; greys the node's connectors; a stable data-node-id.

props.name: Flow.Parallel: align
props.description: Aligns the branches to the end of the widest one.

props.name: Flow.List
props.description: A sequence of nodes inside a parallel branch.

props.name: Flow.Anchor: type / render
props.description: Marks where connectors leave (start) or arrive (end) inside a custom node; both when omitted.

a11y: The flow is a nested list: the diagram is a <ul>, each node an <li>, and each parallel group and branch sequence a nested list, so screen readers announce its order and branches. Connectors are an aria-hidden SVG.

When the diagram overflows, the canvas is a focusable group (name it with aria-label): arrow keys pan by 40 px, Home and End jump to the start and end, and the scrollbars show while it has keyboard focus. Focus moving to a control inside a node pans that control into view.
Panning is immediate (pointer, wheel and keys alike), with no animation or inertia, so reduced motion needs no change.

Fidelity default, contrast on request: the connectors (2.6:1 on white, 4.4:1 in dark) and the node ring (1.2:1 light, 1.5:1 dark) keep the upstream colors; under prefers-contrast: more they rise to 4.7:1 (light) and 7.4:1 or more (dark). In forced colors the connectors follow CanvasText and nodes get an outline (shadows are removed there). Override the --flow-diagram-* variables to raise them for everyone.
Right to left, the flow mirrors: it progresses from the right, the connectors are mirrored and the pan range follows.
docs:
Installed `Flow` (`@/components/ui/flow-diagram`): a directed flow diagram. Nodes are laid out automatically from the JSX tree and joined by rounded connectors; a diagram larger than its container pans by drag, wheel or arrow keys.

```tsx
import { Flow } from "@/components/ui/flow-diagram";

<Flow aria-label="Deploy pipeline">
  <Flow.Node>Build</Flow.Node>
  <Flow.Parallel>
    <Flow.Node>Unit tests</Flow.Node>
    <Flow.Node>Lint</Flow.Node>
  </Flow.Parallel>
  <Flow.Node>Release</Flow.Node>
</Flow>
```

- `Flow.Parallel` branches (its children run side by side); `Flow.List` puts a sequence inside a branch.
- `Flow.Node render={<li className="..." />}` replaces the default card; `Flow.Anchor type="start" | "end"` moves where connectors attach.
- `orientation="vertical"`, `align="center"` and `Flow.Parallel align="end"` change the layout; `disabled` greys the connectors of a node.

Use it from a client component (`Flow.Node` and the other members are properties of `Flow`, which a server component cannot read). It measures its nodes in the browser, so the server render shows the frame and the nodes appear on hydration. Colors and the node radius are the `--flow-diagram-*` variables (light and dark). Name a diagram that can overflow with `aria-label`: it then takes keyboard focus. Right to left, the flow mirrors and progresses from the right.

Ported from Cloudflare's flow components (MIT); the license notice is at the end of every file.
